pass1.sentence: After at least 8 hours without food.
pass1.note: Lab Tests Online UK summary: nothing but water for at least 8 hours (8-10 hours cited). NIDDK says the same (US).

pass1.sentence: A fasting level of 7.0 mmol/L or above indicates diabetes and, without symptoms, is confirmed by a second test on another day.
pass1.note: Diabetes UK page: fasting plasma glucose 7.0 or above; without symptoms at least one more result in the diabetic range on another day.

pass1.sentence: Any time of day; 11.1 mmol/L or above with symptoms suggests diabetes.
pass1.note: Diabetes UK: random venous plasma glucose 11.1 or above; symptomatic cases adequate on one result (trust documents).

pass1.sentence: Fasting tests need at least 8 hours without food, water allowed.
pass1.note: Reworded from '8-12 hours': 12 hours was not retrieved; a UK hospital glucose tolerance protocol uses 11 hours (a different test).

pass1.sentence: Impaired fasting glucose on the World Health Organization definition, a form of prediabetes.
pass1.note: NICE PH38 glossary quoting WHO: IFG is fasting plasma glucose 6.1 to 6.9 mmol/l.

pass1.sentence: NICE flags a fasting level of 5.5 to 6.9 mmol/L as high risk of type 2 diabetes, and US sources start at 5.6, so the lower limit depends on the guideline used
pass1.note: NICE glossary: high risk = fasting plasma glucose 5.5 to 6.9 or HbA1c 42-47. MedlinePlus: IFG 5.6 to 6.9 (search summary).

pass1.sentence: Diabetes if confirmed on a second test, or if symptoms are present
pass1.note: Diabetes UK confirmatory rule; symptomatic single-result rule from NHS trust documents (summary blends).

pass1.sentence: Below 4.0 mmol/L: hypoglycaemia in people with diabetes
pass1.note: NHS 111 Wales: usually below 4 mmol/L; Leeds Community Healthcare and Guy's and St Thomas' say below 4; UCLH uses 3.6.
